captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a woodworking front vise. It features a dark brown fixed block representing a workbench edge, a lighter brown movable jaw, and a metal screw mechanism with a wooden handle. The movable jaw slides horizontally on two parallel metal guide rods, while the handle can be rotated to drive the screw mechanism.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a woodworking front vise with a fixed rear bench block, a movable front jaw, and a lead-screw handle assembly. The front jaw should slide prismatically relative to the fixed block along horizontal guide rods, and the handle should rotate continuously about the central screw axis.
captions.factory: The code defines an ArticulatedObject consisting of three main parts: a fixed bench block (base), a sliding jaw (jaw), and a rotating handle (handle). The bench block is constructed using Box primitives representing the bench top and the vertical fixed jaw. The movable jaw is built from Box primitives representing the jaw plate and its inner block, along with Cylinder primitives for the two horizontal guide rods. The handle part is composed of a central Cylinder for the screw hub, a horizontal Cylinder for the handle bar, and Spheres at each end of the bar. A prismatic articulation is defined between the fixed bench and the sliding jaw, while a continuous revolute articulation is defined between the sliding jaw and the rotating handle.
